name: Question 4
problem:
Find the Laplace transform $Y(s)=L{y(t)}$ for $s>3$ if 

$$
{y}^{′}+y=-8\operatorname{cosh}⁡3t,\,y(0)=1.
$$

You may make use of the following result:

$$
L{\operatorname{cosh}⁡\omega t}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}-{\omega }^{2}},\,s>|\omega |.
$$
worked_solution:
First, we take the Laplace transform of both sides and use the addition and scalar multiplication properties of the Laplace transform:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{y}^{′}+y} & =L{-8\operatorname{cosh}⁡3t} \\ L{{y}^{′}}+L{y} & =-8L{\operatorname{cosh}⁡3t}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate $L{{y}^{′}},$ we use the formula for the Laplace transform of a derivative and the initial condition $y(0)=1:$

$$
L{{y}^{′}}=sL{y}-y(0)=sY(s)-1
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have the following result:

$$
L{\operatorname{cosh}⁡3t}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}-9},\,s>3
$$

Therefore, we can solve for $Y(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{y}^{′}}+L{y} & =-8L{\operatorname{cosh}⁡3t} \\ (sY(s)-1)+Y(s) & =-8(\frac{s}{{s}^{2}-9}) \\ sY(s)+Y(s) & =1-\frac{8s}{{s}^{2}-9} \\ (s+1)Y(s) & =\frac{{s}^{2}-8s-9}{{s}^{2}-9} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{{s}^{2}-8s-9}{({s}^{2}-9)(s+1)}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $s>3,$ we simplify as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Y(s) & =\frac{({s}^{2}-8s-9)}{({s}^{2}-9)(s+1)} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{(s-9)(s+1)}{({s}^{2}-9)(s+1)} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{s-9}{{s}^{2}-9}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Find the Laplace transform Y(s)=L{y(t)} for s>3 if y′+y=−8cosh⁡3t,y(0)=1. You may make use of the following result: L{cosh⁡ωt}=ss2−ω2,s>|ω|.

a
Y(s)=ss2+9
b
Y(s)=ss2−9
c
Y(s)=s−9s2+9
d
Y(s)=s−9s2−9
e
Y(s)=s+9s2−9
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we take the Laplace transform of both sides and use the addition and scalar multiplication properties of the Laplace transform:

L{y′+y}=L{−8cosh⁡3t}L{y′}+L{y}=−8L{cosh⁡3t}

To calculate L{y′}, we use the formula for the Laplace transform of a derivative and the initial condition y(0)=1:

L{y′}=sL{y}−y(0)=sY(s)−1

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have the following result: L{cosh⁡3t}=ss2−9,s>3

Therefore, we can solve for Y(s): L{y′}+L{y}=−8L{cosh⁡3t}(sY(s)−1)+Y(s)=−8(ss2−9)sY(s)+Y(s)=1−8ss2−9(s+1)Y(s)=s2−8s−9s2−9Y(s)=s2−8s−9(s2−9)(s+1)

Since s>3, we simplify as follows:

Y(s)=(s2−8s−9)(s2−9)(s+1)Y(s)=(s−9)(s+1)(s2−9)(s+1)Y(s)=s−9s2−9
